component: TPI LAZARUS U-Boot 2024.04 SATA UEFI v3.9
recorded_by: TPI bring-up host (Dell Wyse 3040, Debian 13): board UART at 1500000 8N1 through a CH343 adapter, board USB-C OTG on the same host, driven remotely over Tailscale

deployment.storage: eMMC loader area, sectors 0-24575 (12 MiB): Forlinx MiniLoader at LBA 64, FIT at LBA 16384
deployment.transport: the board's own USB mass storage: the PC tool switched the board from LOADER with rockusb reset subcode 1, then tpi-uvon wrote the 12 MiB loader area to the eMMC LUN and verified it
deployment.replaced: v3.9-pre2 (FIT edc7d8b05e0133f75a52de7078047efa0ec1f6fed577c7283804064d3028d02d, installed earlier the same day over v3.7 eab1e7bc9cb33094de70f3ed3f47b9df26e3d017f08fdd28da45b5a401ac8361); both saved before being overwritten

pre_flight.method: loaded the chainload image from the FAT ESP of the eMMC into RAM and jumped to it before touching the loader area
pre_flight.observed: the new build printed its banner (Oct 03 2026 - 19:37:10), loaded the environment from eMMC and carried out every check below before the eMMC write

boot_chain_observed: cold boot after a power cut: U-Boot 2024.04-tpi-lazarus-v3.9+ (Oct 03 2026 - 19:37:10 +0000) from eMMC
Loading Environment from MMC... OK; the banner showed the boot order saved by the PC tool
bootflow mmc0 found efi/boot/bootaa64.efi on the eMMC ESP, GRUB 2.12 started Astra Linux 4.7.11 (kernel 6.1.170)
Linux reached the login prompt on ttyS2 at 1500000

console.observed: U-Boot and Linux at 1500000 8N1 on the CH343 without errors; MiniLoader, TF-A and OP-TEE still print at 115200 and show as a few lines of noise

observed: held at power-on: 'RECOVERY pressed: opening the recovery menu'
with no choice the 5 s countdown started LOADER
'Boot order: eMMC first' saved the environment ('Saving Environment to MMC... Writing to MMC(0)... OK') and the menu came back
'Continue normal boot' then booted eMMC first
Ctrl+C in LOADER returned to the menu
host saw 2207:350a 'TPI LAZARUS UVON: LOADER' with the board serial derived from the CPU ID, bcdUSB 2.01 with a BOS holding the USB 2.0 extension, LPM not supported
rockusb reset subcode 1 from the PC tool switched LOADER to mass storage without a reset
host saw 0525:a4a5 'TPI LAZARUS UVON: eMMC, SATA' with LUN 0 eMMC 29.1 GiB and LUN 1 SATA 119.2 GiB
tpi-uvon on the host recognised the board by its serial, the OS on each disk and the saved boot order
eject ended mass storage; the board re-read the environment ('Loading Environment from MMC... OK') and booted in the order just written by the PC ('TPI: boot from microSD', then eMMC)
redundant 64 KiB copies at 12 MiB and 12 MiB + 64 KiB
fw_printenv from libubootenv with a two-line config read tpi_boot_order written by tpi-uvon
written by tpi-uvon on the board and on the PC, and by saveenv from the menu

verified_in_userspace: Astra Linux 4.7.11 from eMMC: Ethernet with a DHCP lease, RTC HYM8563, RS-485 ports ttyUSB0-7 present, OP-TEE region 0x08400000-0x093fffff reserved
not_validated: RKDevTool on Windows; the LOADER protocol was checked with rkdeveloptool only
MaskROM menu entry and rockusb reset subcode 3
booting service media from microSD or USB: none was inserted, only the microSD attempt was observed
Debian on SATA under v3.9: its kernel console is still 115200
rollback: tpi-uvon firmware --file <backup> from Linux on the board, or the PC window over USB; backups of v3.9-pre2 and v3.7 are kept by tpi-uvon in /var/lib/tpi-uvon/firmware-backups
changes_since_v3_7: v3.8 (not released on its own): fixed boot order, SATA first, then eMMC, then any device
boot order configurable as tpi_boot_order and kept in the U-Boot environment on eMMC; only this variable is taken from storage
RECOVERY key opens a menu: RKDevTool LOADER (default after 5 s), service boot from microSD or USB, USB mass storage, normal boot, boot order, MaskROM
USB mass storage with eMMC and SATA as one device (patch ums-lun-devtypes), boot order re-read afterwards
LOADER switched to mass storage from the PC by rockusb reset subcode 1 (patch rockusb-board-reset-flag)
rockusb seen as a LOADER by RKDevTool and rkdeveloptool, Read Flash Info answered (patch rockusb-loader-mode)
